title: The presence rule for two zones is dead code: `auto`, the default mode, is resolved as `on`
claim: ThermalParameters.from_config tests the two-zone mode with `in (TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE)`, and DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE is `auto`, so every entry with no mode key or with `auto` is modelled two-zone whatever keys it holds; the `else` arm that infers the mode from the zone keys is reached only by an unknown mode string. On 4 of 6 configs the default mode and an unknown mode -- which the function's own comment declares the same rule -- give different answers.
mechanism: thermal_model.py:1122-1134: `if two_zone_mode in (ON, DEFAULT): True / elif == OFF: False / else: any(zone key in config)`. The three arms take all three values of const.TWO_ZONE_MODES between them, so the presence rule above them in the comment (`auto ... is the presence rule unchanged; an unknown value is treated as auto`) cannot run for a valid entry. An install that never chose a mode and stores no zone keys -- every single-zone house set up before the mode key, and tests/profiles.py's `house(two_zone=False)` -- is simulated, planned and identified as two zones with the default zone parameters. config_flow._single_zone takes its answer from the same call, so the options flow hides the whole-house loss field on those entries too.

evidence.unit: configs of 6 on which `no mode key` or `auto` answers two_zone_enabled differently from an unknown mode on the same config (no zone keys, and a stored single-zone house: True against False; with zone keys both say True)
evidence.machine: Apple M1 (8 cores), Darwin 27.2.0 arm64, Python 3.14.7 (venv-ci)
evidence.contention_note: shared box during the fan-out, load1 150-270; the number is a static or behavioural count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: the classmethod re-executed in memory with `(const.TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, const.DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE)` replaced by `(const.TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON,)` (m6_two_zone_auto.py --perturb); the static twin: m6_stmt.py's exhausted_else row for thermal_model.py leaves the census

metric_definition: configs (zone keys absent, present, or a stored single-zone house) x (no mode key, auto) whose two_zone_enabled differs from the same config under an unknown mode string
phenomenon_property: An if/elif chain over one subject whose arms take every value of the enumeration it tests has no further arm carrying logic: an `else` that holds a rule is reachable by a valid value, or the rule is not in force.

null_control.note: the explicit modes are untouched on all three configs (on -> True, off -> False), and with zone keys present the default mode and the unknown mode agree (2 of 2)

proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py: `auto` falls through to the presence rule (the membership test names ON alone). Every golden and scenario built on a config with no zone keys moves back to one zone.
expected_golden_drift: every fixture whose config has no zone keys and no explicit mode: it is two-zone in this tree and single-zone after the fix
